paragraphs.title: The Angels Arrive and Lot Welcomes Them

easy.question: Who arrived in Sodom at the beginning of the passage?
easy.explanation: The first verse says, “And there came two angels to Sodom.”

easy.question: Where was Lot sitting?
easy.explanation: The passage says that Lot was sitting at the gate of Sodom.

easy.question: What did Lot prepare for his guests?
easy.explanation: Lot made them a feast and baked unleavened bread, and they ate.

medium.question: What did Lot do when he saw the angels?
answers: He rose to meet them and bowed down
He went inside and shut the door
He sent them into the street
medium.explanation: When Lot saw them, he rose to meet them and bowed with his face toward the ground.

medium.question: What does the phrase “he pressed upon them greatly” mean in context?
medium.explanation: The phrase means that Lot strongly and persistently urged them to enter his house.

medium.question: Why did Lot invite the guests into his house?
answers: So they could teach him the law
So they would remain in the city for a long time
So they could stay the night, wash their feet, and continue on their way
medium.explanation: Lot offered them lodging, washing, an early start, and continuation of their journey.

challenge.question: What can we learn from the fact that the angels first said they would stay in the street but eventually entered Lot’s house?
answers: Lot persuaded them to accept his hospitality
They did not want to stay anywhere
They asked Lot to leave Sodom
challenge.explanation: At first they declined, but after Lot urged them strongly, they agreed to enter his house.

challenge.question: What does the combination of “at evening” and “ye shall rise up early, and go on your ways” suggest?
answers: They arrived in the morning and stayed all day
The visit was intended to last only one night
Lot asked them to live with him
challenge.explanation: They arrived in the evening, and Lot offered them a brief overnight stay.

challenge.question: What was Lot asking when he said, “turn in, I pray you, into your servant’s house”?
answers: Come to his house and stay with him
challenge.explanation: Here, “turn in” means to leave the road and come into Lot’s house.

questions.question: What can we learn from the fact that the angels first said they would stay in the street but eventually entered Lot’s house?
answers: Lot persuaded them to accept his hospitality
They did not want to stay anywhere
They asked Lot to leave Sodom
questions.explanation: At first they declined, but after Lot urged them strongly, they agreed to enter his house.

questions.question: What does the combination of “at evening” and “ye shall rise up early, and go on your ways” suggest?
answers: They arrived in the morning and stayed all day
The visit was intended to last only one night
Lot asked them to live with him
questions.explanation: They arrived in the evening, and Lot offered them a brief overnight stay.

questions.question: What was Lot asking when he said, “turn in, I pray you, into your servant’s house”?
answers: Come to his house and stay with him
questions.explanation: Here, “turn in” means to leave the road and come into Lot’s house.

paragraphs.title: The Men of Sodom Surround the House

easy.question: Who surrounded Lot’s house?
easy.explanation: The passage says that the men of the city, the men of Sodom, surrounded the house.

easy.question: Who took part in surrounding the house?
easy.explanation: The passage emphasizes that people of every age were present, from young to old.

easy.question: What did Lot do after going out to the men of the city?
answers: He shut the door behind him
easy.explanation: The verse says that Lot shut the door after himself.

medium.question: What happened before Lot and the angels went to sleep?
answers: The men of the city surrounded the house
medium.explanation: Before they lay down, the men of the city surrounded the house.

medium.question: What does “compassed the house round” mean?
medium.explanation: The phrase says that the men were all around the house.

medium.question: Why did Lot go out to the men of the city?
answers: To invite them to a feast
medium.explanation: The men called to Lot, and he went out to them at the door.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by the phrase “both old and young”?
answers: Only the city’s leaders were there
People of every age took part
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes a broad range of ages, from the young to the old.

challenge.question: What order of events is described in the sixth verse?
answers: Lot shut the door and then went out
The angels went out while Lot stayed inside
Lot went out to the men and then shut the door behind him
challenge.explanation: Lot went out first, and then he shut the door behind him.

challenge.question: What does the repeated phrase “the men of the city, even the men of Sodom” suggest?
answers: The problem involved the people of Sodom as a whole, not one individual
Only one man came from the city
The men did not know where the house was
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that a large group of Sodom’s citizens was involved.

questions.question: What is emphasized by the phrase “both old and young”?
answers: Only the city’s leaders were there
People of every age took part
questions.explanation: The phrase describes a broad range of ages, from the young to the old.

questions.question: What order of events is described in the sixth verse?
answers: Lot shut the door and then went out

Lot went out to the men and then shut the door behind him
questions.explanation: Lot went out first, and then he shut the door behind him.

questions.question: What does the repeated phrase “the men of the city, even the men of Sodom” suggest?
answers: The problem involved the people of Sodom as a whole, not one individual

questions.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that a large group of Sodom’s citizens was involved.

paragraphs.title: Lot Tries to Protect His Guests

easy.question: Who asked the wicked men not to harm the guests?
easy.explanation: Lot said, “I pray you, brethren, do not so wickedly.”

easy.question: What did the men of the city try to do to Lot’s door?
easy.explanation: They came near to break the door.

easy.question: What did the men do to the people outside the house?
answers: They drove them from the city
easy.explanation: They struck the men with blindness, so they could not find the door.

medium.question: Why did Lot ask the men of the city not to harm his guests?
answers: The guests had come under his roof, so he felt responsible for protecting them
They had promised him a gift
medium.explanation: Lot said that the men had come under the shadow of his roof and protection.

medium.question: What happened after the men tried to break the door?
answers: Lot went out and joined them
The men pulled Lot inside and shut the door
The men of the city left immediately
medium.explanation: The men reached out, pulled Lot into the house, and shut the door.

medium.question: What does “they pressed sore upon the man” mean?
answers: They begged or pressured him insistently
They quickly ran away from him
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the men’s forceful and persistent pressure on Lot.

challenge.question: What did the men mean by saying, “This one fellow came in to sojourn, and he will needs be a judge”?
answers: They resented that Lot, a resident alien, presumed to judge them
They admitted that Lot was the city’s king
They asked Lot to teach them about justice
challenge.explanation: They portrayed Lot as an outsider who had come to live there yet dared to criticize them.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the phrase “both small and great”?
answers: People of every age and status searched for the door
challenge.explanation: The phrase means that everyone, from the least to the greatest, was involved.

challenge.question: Why could the men not find the door after being struck with blindness?
answers: Their sight was impaired and they could not find their way
challenge.explanation: Their blindness prevented them from locating the entrance.

questions.question: What did the men mean by saying, “This one fellow came in to sojourn, and he will needs be a judge”?
answers: They resented that Lot, a resident alien, presumed to judge them

They asked Lot to teach them about justice
questions.explanation: They portrayed Lot as an outsider who had come to live there yet dared to criticize them.

questions.question: What can we infer from the phrase “both small and great”?
answers: People of every age and status searched for the door
questions.explanation: The phrase means that everyone, from the least to the greatest, was involved.

questions.question: Why could the men not find the door after being struck with blindness?
answers: Their sight was impaired and they could not find their way
questions.explanation: Their blindness prevented them from locating the entrance.

paragraphs.title: The Warning and Departure from Sodom

easy.question: Who told Lot to bring his family out of the city?
answers: The men who had come to him
easy.explanation: The men, who were angels, told Lot to bring his family out.

easy.question: What did Lot tell his sons-in-law to do?
easy.explanation: Lot told them, “Up, get you out of this place.”

easy.question: Where did the men bring Lot and his family?
easy.explanation: They brought them out and set them outside the city.

medium.question: Why were the men going to destroy the place?
answers: Because the cry against its people had become great before the Lord
medium.explanation: They said that the Lord had sent them to destroy the place because of the great cry against it.

medium.question: What does “he lingered” mean in context?
answers: He delayed and did not leave at once
He became angry with the men
medium.explanation: Lot did not leave immediately, so the men had to take him by the hand and lead him out.

medium.question: What happened after Lot warned his sons-in-law about the city’s destruction?
answers: They left the city at once
They called the men of the city
medium.explanation: Lot seemed to his sons-in-law as one who was mocking.

challenge.question: What can we understand from “his sons-in-law, which married his daughters”?
answers: Lot spoke to men connected to him through his daughters’ marriages
Lot spoke to his young sons
Lot spoke to the city’s leaders
challenge.explanation: The phrase identifies the men who had married Lot’s daughters.

challenge.question: Why did the angels hurry Lot at daybreak?
answers: They wanted to invite the city’s men to a feast
Destruction was near, so he and his family had to leave quickly
Lot asked to remain until evening
challenge.explanation: The angels urged Lot to leave because the city’s destruction was about to occur.

challenge.question: What does the contrast between Lot’s hesitation and the men’s action emphasize?
answers: Lot wanted the city destroyed, but the men objected
Lot did not know the way, and the men wanted to learn it
Lot struggled to escape, and the men rescued him through the Lord’s mercy
challenge.explanation: Because Lot lingered, the men took hold of him and his family and brought them out, showing the Lord’s mercy.

answers: Lot spoke to men connected to him through his daughters’ marriages
Lot spoke to his young sons
Lot spoke to the city’s leaders

answers: They wanted to invite the city’s men to a feast

answers: Lot wanted the city destroyed, but the men objected

paragraphs.title: The Escape and the City of Zoar

easy.question: What did the angels command Lot to do?
easy.explanation: The angels told Lot to escape so that he would live.

easy.question: Where did Lot ask to escape?
easy.explanation: Lot asked to flee to the nearby little city.

easy.question: What was the name of the city Lot wanted to reach?
easy.explanation: The passage says that the city was called Zoar.

medium.question: Why did the angels tell Lot not to look behind him?
answers: So he would not stop along the way
So he could find the city
So he could see the mountain
medium.explanation: Lot had to escape quickly without stopping or looking back.

medium.question: What does “thou hast magnified thy mercy” mean in context?
answers: You have accepted my request and shown me great kindness
medium.explanation: Lot says that the angel accepted his request and showed him mercy by saving his life.

medium.question: What did Lot ask for after saying he could not escape to the mountain?
answers: To escape to a nearby little city
medium.explanation: Lot asked to flee to the nearby city because he thought he could not reach the mountain.

Lot had to reach Zoar before the destruction began
Lot was not allowed to enter Zoar
challenge.explanation: The angel said he could do nothing until Lot arrived there, so destruction would wait until then.

challenge.question: Why was the city called “Zoar,” according to the passage?
answers: Because it was a little city
Because it was on a mountain
challenge.explanation: The name is connected with Lot’s description of the city as small or little.

challenge.question: What changed between the angels’ first command and Lot’s request?
answers: Lot was first told to flee to the mountain, but was later allowed to flee to Zoar
Lot was first told to remain, but was later told to return
Lot was first allowed to look back, but was later forbidden to escape

answers: The city would be spared because Lot asked

Lot was not allowed to enter Zoar
questions.explanation: The angel said he could do nothing until Lot arrived there, so destruction would wait until then.

answers: Because it was a little city
Because it was on a mountain

answers: Lot was first told to flee to the mountain, but was later allowed to flee to Zoar
Lot was first told to remain, but was later told to return
Lot was first allowed to look back, but was later forbidden to escape

She looked back while the fire was falling
She looked back after Lot had entered Zoar

easy.question: What did Abraham see when he looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah?

easy.question: Whom did God send out from the destruction?

medium.question: What did Abraham see after looking toward Sodom, Gomorrah, and the plain?

medium.question: What does “smoke of the country” mean in context?
medium.explanation: The comparison to furnace smoke shows that smoke was rising from the land after the destruction.

Lot rescued Abraham and was saved in return
Abraham told Lot to leave afterward

paragraphs.title: Lot and His Daughters in the Cave

easy.question: Where did Lot go up from Zoar?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Lot went up from Zoar and dwelt in the mountain.

easy.question: Who was with Lot?
easy.explanation: The verse says that his two daughters were with him.

easy.question: Where did Lot and his two daughters live?
easy.explanation: The verse says that he and his two daughters dwelt in a cave.

medium.question: Why did Lot not remain in Zoar?
answers: Because the city was far away
Because he was afraid to live in Zoar
Because his daughters asked to leave

medium.question: What is the order of events in the verse?

Lot stayed in Zoar and then went down to a cave
Lot went up from Zoar to the mountain and then lived in a cave

He wanted to return to Zoar
He moved to a large city

easy.question: What did the firstborn say about their father?

easy.question: What did the daughters propose doing to their father?

medium.question: Why did the daughters think they needed to act?

Their father commanded them to do it
They wanted to leave the land

medium.question: What does “Come” mean in the phrase “Come, let us make our father drink wine”?

medium.question: What was the purpose of the daughters’ plan?

easy.question: When did the event described in the verse take place?

easy.question: Which daughter went in and lay with her father?

easy.question: What did the daughters give their father to drink?

easy.question: Which daughter lay with their father on the second night?

medium.question: What does “that we may preserve seed of our father” mean?
